questions.answer: Treating \((x+1)\) as a single unit (power rule for a linear inner function): \(\int(x+1)^3\,dx = \frac{(x+1)^4}{4}+C\).

questions.q: Find \(\int(2x-1)^5\,dx\), treating \((2x-1)\) as a linear inner function.
questions.answer: \(\int(2x-1)^5\,dx=\frac{(2x-1)^6}{6\cdot2}+C=\frac{(2x-1)^6}{12}+C\) (dividing by the derivative of the inner function, \(2\)).

Level 2 · MediumSolve the transcendental equation analytically for \(x\) in exact form using natural logarithms: \(3^{2x+1} = 5^{x-2}.\)
questions.answer: Take the natural logarithm of both sides: \(\ln(3^{2x+1}) = \ln(5^{x-2}).\) Apply the power law of logarithms: \((2x + 1)\ln 3 = (x - 2)\ln 5.\) Distribute: \(2x\ln 3 + \ln 3 = x\ln 5 - 2\ln 5.\) Collect all terms containing \(x\) on one side: \(2x\ln 3 - x\ln 5 = -\ln 3 - 2\ln 5 \Rightarrow x(2\ln 3 - \ln 5) = -(\ln 3 + 2\ln 5).\) Simplify logarithmic coefficients: \(2\ln 3 = \ln 9\) and \(2\ln 5 = \ln 25\): \(x(\ln 9 - \ln 5) = -(\ln 3 + \ln 25) \Rightarrow x\ln\left(\frac{9}{5}\right) = -\ln(75).\) Solve for \(x\): \(x = \mathbf{\frac{-\ln(75)}{\ln(9/5)}} = \mathbf{\frac{\ln(1/75)}{\ln(1.8)}}.\)
questions.explanation: Take the natural logarithm of both sides: \(\ln(3^{2x+1}) = \ln(5^{x-2}).\) Apply the power law of logarithms: \((2x + 1)\ln 3 = (x - 2)\ln 5.\) Distribute: \(2x\ln 3 + \ln 3 = x\ln 5 - 2\ln 5.\) Collect all terms containing \(x\) on one side: \(2x\ln 3 - x\ln 5 = -\ln 3 - 2\ln 5 \Rightarrow x(2\ln 3 - \ln 5) = -(\ln 3 + 2\ln 5).\) Simplify logarithmic coefficients: \(2\ln 3 = \ln 9\) and \(2\ln 5 = \ln 25\): \(x(\ln 9 - \ln 5) = -(\ln 3 + \ln 25) \Rightarrow x\ln\left(\frac{9}{5}\right) = -\ln(75).\) Solve for \(x\): \(x = \mathbf{\frac{-\ln(75)}{\ln(9/5)}} = \mathbf{\frac{\ln(1/75)}{\ln(1.8)}}.\)

questions.answer: Substitute \(u = \ln x\). The derivative is \(du = \frac{1}{x}\,dx\). The integral simplifies directly to: \(\int \cos(u)\,du = \sin(u) + C = \sin(\ln x) + C\)

questions.q: Which of the following series converges?
questions.answer: \(\sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n \ln{\left(n \right)}^{2}}\) converges by integral test. The others diverge: \(\sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{1}{2 n + 1}\) by limit comparison with 1/n; \(\sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \left(1 + \frac{1}{n}\right)^{n}\) by nth-term test (terms → e); \(\sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{n}{n^{2} + 1}\) by limit comparison with 1/n.
questions.explanation: \(\sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n \ln{\left(n \right)}^{2}}\) converges by integral test. The others diverge: \(\sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{1}{2 n + 1}\) by limit comparison with 1/n; \(\sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \left(1 + \frac{1}{n}\right)^{n}\) by nth-term test (terms → e); \(\sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{n}{n^{2} + 1}\) by limit comparison with 1/n.

questions.q: Which of the following series diverges?
questions.answer: \(\sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{1}{2 n + 1}\) diverges by limit comparison with 1/n. The others converge: \(\sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \left(\frac{n}{2 n + 1}\right)^{n}\) by root test (limit 1/2); \(\sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{1}{n^{2} + 1}\) by comparison with p-series (p = 2); \(\sum_{n=2}^{\infty} n^{- n} n!\) by ratio test (limit 1/e < 1).

questions.q: Consider the function \(f(x) = x^2\). What is the value of the definite integral \(\int_{0}^{3} f(x) dx\)?
questions.answer: The integral of \(f(x) = x^2\) is \(\frac{x^3}{3}\). Evaluating this from 0 to 3 gives: \(\left[\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{0}^{3} = \frac{3^3}{3} - \frac{0^3}{3} = \frac{27}{3} - 0 = 9\). Therefore, the value of the definite integral is 9.
questions.explanation: The integral of \(f(x) = x^2\) is \(\frac{x^3}{3}\). Evaluating this from 0 to 3 gives: \(\left[\frac{x^3}{3}\right]_{0}^{3} = \frac{3^3}{3} - \frac{0^3}{3} = \frac{27}{3} - 0 = 9\). Therefore, the value of the definite integral is 9.
